content.content: When the deccy CLI is invoked as `deccy discard <handle>...` — a single verb, `discard`, in the verb position, with the handles as that verb's only arguments — it shall discard exactly one open draft per handle, the handle being the only key that addresses a draft, with no node id, edit or workspace standing in its place, and shall end each such draft without landing it; if any handle names no open record, then the CLI shall refuse the whole invocation without discarding any draft; in either case the invocation shall write no node and no change.
content.rationale: This node states the discard invocation in the EARS requirement form, because the commitment is a required behaviour of the CLI rather than code or a stored artifact; its licence is the prose surface kxyznwxu, the landed-end requirement slwvtspu and the prose store twpvqstu, and each edge is a natural-to-structured reading applied by reading the sentence against the recorded nodes, with nothing to run. The sentence names the invocation `deccy discard <handle>...` and reads each clause off a prerequisite. `a single verb, discard, in the verb position, with the handles as that verb's only arguments` is the surface's one-verb form and its handle list (wzmmmmsw, kxyznwxu), and it is as much as the requirement says about the surface: it does not answer the argument surface, the empty call, or any output, refusal wording, stream, exit status or help text. `the handle being the only key that addresses a draft, with no node id, edit or workspace standing in its place` is owyntkvw read as the argument's meaning: the record's identity is its handle, while the node, the edit and the workspace are references the record carries, so a node id is a key that names no open record and is refused. `exactly one open draft per handle` is the subject set — one record and therefore one draft per key, and only an `open` record is a subject (tvxspkyy), with a landed record terminal and a handle the directory does not name a record that is not there (twpvqstu). `shall end each such draft without landing it` is slwvtspu's end stated as the response of the accepted call. `if any handle names no open record, then the CLI shall refuse the whole invocation without discarding any draft` is the one-answer rule read off the subject set (wzmmmmsw, owyntkvw): a call carrying a handle that names no open record has no subject set it can answer, so it is refused whole rather than half-answered, and no draft is ended. `in either case the invocation shall write no node and no change` is slwvtspu's operation boundary, stated for the refusal as well as for the discard. The sentence stops where the surface's scope stops: it does not decide what becomes of the record document (twpvqstu), of the draft's workspace, directory or change (vzposmvm, vxltqruo), what a refusal says or exits with, whether a drifted draft is refused — it is not, because the sentence judges only whether a handle names an open record — how a handle is formed or minted, or what help text the verb carries. Each of those can change without changing this sentence, and the sentence can change in wording without changing any of them.
